owner: akiendelllinux_cc_0 (CC) gates writes. The DESIGN is Akien's and is being RESTORED, not authored.
intention: Restore Akien's memory store design as the shape Cairn builds on, and settle the questions it still leaves open — including calving. The design: ONE node list per database; a table per tree; tree links are `table.leaf`; instant node access with no searching; two sets of trees able to index one node set; a tree that grows past its bound CALVES; the SHEAR renumbers leaf addresses along the split.
why: AKIEN'S RULING, 2026-07-26: 'i designed my system because just the reading, nothing else, was overwhelming the usual way of doing it. it wasn't theoretical, it was an experiencial adaptation. if you can't guarantee that it's faster than my solution, we have to go back to mine.' CC cannot guarantee it — there is NO measurement anywhere in the tree comparing the two, no benchmark and no threshold. His design came from load he actually hit; the replacement (MAP.md:527, 'baked in 2026-07-14') came from a design conversation and has never been tested against anything. Law 3 puts the burden on the replacement and the replacement has not carried it. SECOND why, and the sharper one: he can no longer EXPLAIN what the system does, which for him is disqualifying on its own — 'i need to be able to understand and explain to others what we're doing and why at that level.' The cause is measurable: his vocabulary was kept and its meanings changed under it. `calving` survives as a word and now means 'insert a tree row' (MAP.md:529) instead of 'split a tree that grew past its bound'. `the embedding IS the path` survives as a sentence and was read as vectors. Nothing scans as missing, because all the words are still there.

what_was_replaced.survived: ONE node list per database (MAP.md:528, 'nodes ... in ONE logical table'). Two tree-sets indexing one node set — and reinforced by the asymmetric-indexing ruling in held-librarian.
what_was_replaced.replaced: A TABLE PER TREE — MAP.md:528-532 makes trees first-class ROWS and states 'trees never get independent tables'. `table.leaf` LINKS — replaced by an edges table, so you look a node up rather than addressing it. INSTANT ACCESS is weakened to an index lookup: same big-O in practice, different in kind.
what_was_replaced.dropped_with_no_replacement: The BOUND and the SHEAR. Physical calving was demoted to 'Postgres partitioning by tree_id when scale demands' — no threshold, no trigger, no shear. That is a deferral in the shape of a plan.
what_was_replaced.the_stated_reason_and_ccs_read: MAP's why for collapsing per-tree tables: cross-tree edges must be as cheap as within-tree ones, for cross-domain search and cross-tree invalidation. CC's read, flagged as a READ and not a ruling: that objection is weak against THIS design specifically, because a `table.leaf` link already carries its table, so a cross-tree link is just a leaf address with a different table part. The objection assumes you must SEARCH for edges, which is the exact thing the addressing eliminates.

traces_to: Law 3 — the replacement is unmeasured and the original came from measured experience; the burden sits with the replacement.

Law 1 — TheIgors' memory design is already written down (design docs, tickets, tests). Re-deriving it by conversation is the defect; reading it is the fix. This node's first child is a READ, not a design session.
Law 7 — a record of truth never collapses. The graph is the record; a vector index over it is a derived cache that may be freely calved and rebuilt.
memory build-to-the-tool-naming — a term must be derivable from its native use. Reusing `calving` for a different operation broke exactly that, inside Akien's own vocabulary.

gates.prove_gate: proof gate — and see the falsifier: the proof must run at REAL scale, not charter scale.

falsifier: The restored design must be measured AT THE SCALE IT WAS DESIGNED FOR. TheIgors' word graph was ~2.5M nodes; Cairn's largest live measurement to date is 66 records across 14 histories. A load test at 2.5M nodes must show node access that does not degrade with graph size — that is the property the whole design exists to deliver, and the property 'the reading alone was overwhelming' was the symptom of losing. If the restored design does not hold at 2.5M, it is not the design that solved his problem and this reopens. A hollow build — proving the shape on a few hundred rows — fails this outright.
horizon: The design settles when the open questions below are answered by Akien and the load test has run. Not before.
open_questions: THE BOUND: 5K or 1000? Akien said a tree calves past 5K nodes. TheIgors' own ticket reads 'Calving trigger — on write, calve if tree exceeds 1000 nodes'. His to rule, and the discrepancy may itself be informative (a revised threshold, or two different bounds for size and depth).

THE SHEAR AND INBOUND LINKS — ASKED, NOT YET ANSWERED. When a shear renumbers leaf addresses, what happens to inbound links from OTHER trees pointing at the renumbered leaves? Fixed up along the shear, indirected through something stable, or does the asymmetric-indexing rule (private-down by default, specialists index the commons) mean inbound cross-tree links only ever point at things that do not shear?

EDGES: STORED, DERIVED, OR BOTH? MAP.md:527 stores edges in a table; held-librarian concluded they are derived from vectors (now corrected at source — that conclusion was CC's, not Akien's). CC's proposed reconciliation, UNRULED: two edge KINDS — articulated edges STORED (directed, typed, what invalidation propagates along) and similarity edges DERIVED from the graph walk. Akien's to settle.

TWO THINGS NAMED CALVING in TheIgors itself — graph calving (tree splitting) and a 'serial-calving counter' in node_id.py for ID uniqueness, flagged in their own docs as 'distinct but related naming'. Which name survives into Cairn.
